drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Counsel — We can accept a cash-free, debt-free structure with an agreed working-capital target, a post-closing true-up and independent-accountant resolution. We have also expanded the representations and closing conditions. To balance those protections, we propose a 10% escrow for 12 months, a defined diligence period, and customary indemnity limitations. The attached language preserves the thirty-day closing timetable without an open-ended satisfaction condition. Please confirm agreement on these principles so we can finalize the price, target, disclosure schedules and escrow arrangements before signing.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. Buyer shall purchase the Shares at the base purchase price expressly agreed by the parties in writing before signing (the Base Price), on a cash-free, debt-free basis and assuming delivery of an agreed normalized level of working capital. Before signing, the parties shall agree a schedule specifying the Base Price, working-capital target, definitions of cash, indebtedness and working capital, and applicable accounting policies, together with an illustrative calculation. The purchase price shall equal the Base Price, plus closing cash, less closing indebtedness, and increased or decreased by the amount by which closing working capital exceeds or falls below the target, without double counting. Seller shall deliver an estimated closing statement at least three business days before Closing, and the closing payment shall be calculated using that statement. Buyer shall deliver its proposed final statement within sixty days after Closing; otherwise Seller’s estimated statement shall become final. Seller shall have thirty days to review and object, with reasonable access to supporting records and personnel. Uncontested items shall become final. Following twenty days of good-faith consultation, unresolved accounting items shall be submitted to a mutually appointed independent accountant acting as an expert, not an arbitrator. The accountant shall apply the agreed definitions and accounting policies, determine only disputed items within the parties’ respective proposed amounts, and issue a binding determination absent manifest error. Its fees shall be allocated in proportion to each party’s unsuccessful disputed amounts. Any final adjustment shall be paid within five business days. At Closing, 10% of the estimated purchase price shall be deposited with a mutually acceptable escrow agent for twelve months solely to secure Seller’s indemnity obligations; the balance shall be paid to Seller in immediately available funds. At expiry, the escrow shall be released to Seller except for amounts reasonably necessary to cover specifically described, good-faith claims notified before expiry, which shall be released promptly upon resolution.
edits.name: Purchase price mechanics and escrow

edits.text: 2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days after signing, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the benefiting party of the following conditions: receipt of required consents specifically identified in an agreed schedule at signing; Seller’s delivery of good title to the Shares free of liens, with any applicable liens released concurrently with Closing; accuracy of Seller’s representations at Closing, except for inaccuracies that would not individually or in the aggregate be material to the acquired business, provided that representations concerning authority and title to the Shares shall be accurate in all respects; material performance of each party’s obligations; and absence of any legal prohibition on Closing. Buyer shall complete diligence within ten business days after signing. The diligence condition shall be deemed satisfied unless Buyer gives notice within that period identifying a previously undisclosed matter materially adverse to the acquired business and explaining its basis in reasonable detail. Seller shall provide reasonable access to requested diligence materials promptly, and the parties shall work in good faith to resolve any timely identified matter before the scheduled Closing. There shall be no financing condition. Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy the closing conditions and shall not rely on a failure caused by its own breach. If Closing has not occurred by the thirtieth day after signing, either party may terminate by written notice, unless that party’s breach caused the failure to close; termination shall not affect accrued rights for breach. The parties may extend that date by written agreement.
edits.name: Defined closing conditions and diligence period

edits.text: 3. REPRESENTATIONS. Seller represents at signing and Closing, subject to exceptions fairly disclosed in disclosure schedules delivered and agreed before signing, that: (a) Seller has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and owns the Shares free of liens other than those to be released at Closing; (b) the delivered financial statements have been prepared consistently with the accounting principles identified in the schedules and fairly present, in all material respects, the acquired business’s financial position and results, subject, for interim statements, to normal year-end adjustments and absence of footnotes; (c) all material tax returns required to be filed have been timely filed and are accurate in all material respects, all material taxes due have been paid, and no material tax dispute is pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened in writing; (d) the acquired business complies in all material respects with applicable laws and holds all material permits required for its operations; (e) the schedules identify all material contracts, copies have been provided to Buyer, each is in force, and neither the acquired business nor, to Seller’s knowledge, any counterparty is in material default; (f) no material litigation is pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened in writing against the acquired business, and no material outstanding judgment or order affects it; and (g) the acquired business has no material liabilities required to be reflected or reserved in its financial statements under the agreed accounting principles except those so reflected or reserved, fairly disclosed in the schedules, or incurred in the ordinary course since the latest financial statement date and not arising from breach of contract or law. Seller’s knowledge means the actual knowledge of the officers identified in the schedules after reasonable inquiry of personnel responsible for the relevant subject matter. Buyer represents that it has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and will have sufficient immediately available funds at Closing.
edits.name: Expanded and qualified representations

edits.text: 4. INDEMNITY. Following Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for actual losses resulting from breach of Seller’s representations or covenants, taxes attributable to periods ending on or before Closing (with straddle-period taxes allocated under an agreed schedule), and any specifically identified indemnified matters agreed in the disclosure schedules. Buyer shall indemnify Seller for actual losses resulting from breach of Buyer’s representations or covenants. General representations shall survive for twelve months after Closing; Seller’s authority and title representations and tax obligations shall survive until sixty days after the applicable limitation period expires. Covenants shall survive in accordance with their terms. Claims for breach of general representations shall be recoverable only to the extent aggregate recoverable losses exceed 1% of the final purchase price and shall be capped at 10% of the final purchase price, with the escrow as Buyer’s sole recourse for such claims. The basket, general cap and escrow-only limitation shall not apply to Seller’s authority or title representations, taxes, covenants or specifically agreed indemnified matters; Seller’s aggregate liability for all claims shall nevertheless not exceed the final purchase price, except for Seller’s actual fraud, for which no contractual limitation shall apply. No party may recover twice for the same loss, recover amounts already reflected in the purchase-price adjustment, or recover punitive damages except to the extent payable to a third party. Recoverable losses shall be reduced by insurance proceeds and third-party recoveries actually received, net of reasonable recovery costs. Each indemnified party shall take reasonable steps to mitigate losses. Claims must be notified with reasonable particulars before the applicable survival period expires; timely notified claims shall survive until resolved. The indemnifying party may control the defense of a third-party claim with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified party, provided it acknowledges its indemnity obligation and the claim does not involve criminal allegations, a material conflict of interest or material nonmonetary relief. No settlement imposing an admission, nonmonetary obligation or unreimbursed payment on the indemnified party may be entered without its consent. These indemnities shall be the exclusive post-Closing monetary remedy for matters covered by this Agreement, except for actual fraud and purchase-price adjustments; rights to specific performance and other equitable relief remain available.
edits.name: Indemnity scope, survival and limitations

receiver.message_back: We agree in principle to the cash-free, debt-free pricing mechanics and thirty-day closing timetable, subject to definitive documentation, but require a 15% escrow and general-representation cap for eighteen months, a 0.5% tipping basket, direct Seller recourse for any escrow shortfall, and escrow security for purchase-price adjustments as well as indemnities. Buyer’s ten-business-day diligence period must run from delivery of all reasonably requested materials, with an extension of the outside date for Seller delay and an express Buyer termination right for a timely identified, unresolved materially adverse diligence matter; price, target, schedules and escrow terms remain subject to agreement before signing.
